subject: lists of markers with and without distorted segregation

messages.author: c4390b997ff96dbb
messages.subject: lists of markers with and without distorted segregation
parts:
I am running analyses on a cluster because of the size of my dataset.

 

I want to generate two output files,

1) a one column list of the markers that have been dropped and

2) a one column list of the markers that are retained

 

I wrote and it seemed to work

 

gt <- geno.table(All_q50C50)

#gt[gt$P.value < 0.05/totmar(All_q50C50),]

todrop<- rownames(gt[gt$P.value < 1e-10,])

#DisMarkers.txt <- print(todrop, as.table=TRUE)

lapply(todrop, write, "DisMarkers.txt", append=TRUE, ncolumns=5)

tokeep<- rownames(gt[gt$P.value >= 1e-10,])

lapply(tokeep, write, "NoDisMarkers.txt", append=TRUE, ncolumns=5)

 

there are 1083 markers in the DisMarkers.txt

there are 1585 markers in the NoDisMarkers.txt

dataset has 2668 markers

 

when I look at the list generated after

gt[gt$P.value < 0.05/totmar(All_q50C50),]

I expected the list to be the same as the list in DisMarkers.txt

but there are 1438 markers listed and the list has markers from both DisMarkers.txt and the NoDisMarkers.txt

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] lists of markers with and without distorted segregation
parts:
I don't really understand your code. In particular, lapply seems unnecessary.

I would just do:

gt <- geno.table(All_q50C50)
todrop <- rownames(gt)[gt$P.value < 1e-10]
tokeep <- rownames(gt)[gt$P.value >= 1e-10]
write(todrop, "DisMarkers.txt", ncolumns=1)
write(tokeep, "NoDisMarkers.txt", ncolumns=1)

karl
